note: [agent-bulk] This is the rubric's literal over-clustering case -- the shower swallows a straight minimum-ionising stem, and the stem is 125 cm long. Vertex judged from a --vtx-span 60 re-capture (event_half_span_cm 173.8 -- correction 5) and it is FINE: two pdg-2212 segments, 83021 (30.2 cm) and 83023 (9.0 cm), both have dvtx 0.0 and in the close-in view they converge on the star with the shower's line leaving the same point -- a hadronic vertex, no complaint. VERDICT on 85025 (412.4 MeV, 6 segments, table length 140.1 cm, the ONLY shower in scope): over-clustered, certain. In the 3-D view at az-055-el+20 AND again at az-055-el+65 the yellow member set is ONE long, thin, perfectly straight line of uniform width running about 140 cm from the X to a small hook at the far end -- no cone, no widening, no branching anywhere along it. An EM shower cannot be 140 cm long at constant width. The member list says the same thing: the seed 85025 is a 1.31 cm 3-point stub 5.5 cm from the vertex, and the 412.4 MeV comes from 10008 -- a 125.09 cm, 208-point, pdg-13 segment absorbed by pass4_angle at 14.8 cm / 3.2 deg -- plus 10005 (9.95 cm, at the muon's FAR end, dvtx 138.3, absorbed by pass4_proximity at 132.8 cm / 9.8 deg; that is the hook, most likely the decay electron). 412.4 MeV over 140.1 cm is 2.9 MeV/cm, MIP-like. MARKS: 10008 OUT and 10005 OUT of 85025. Per correction 7 these are not equal but both are strong: 10008 is the whole muon and carries essentially all the energy; 10005 is its far-end hook and only makes sense to keep if 10008 is kept. I did NOT mark the three small bridge members -- 84024 (pdg 2212, 0.46 cm, 8.1 cm / 2.9 deg), 10004 (2.96 cm, 12.3 cm / 2.8 deg) and 76015 (pdg 13, 0.37 cm, 20.8 cm / 18.9 deg) -- because with the muon removed what is left is a 1.3 cm seed and three specks and the object arguably should not be a shower at all; those three are the ones I would let the owner move either way. AN EQUALLY DEFENSIBLE ALTERNATIVE VERDICT would have been 'not an EM shower', since the whole object is a muon; I chose the clustering bucket because the rubric names this exact case under over-clustered and because a clustering verdict is the more actionable one. UNDER-CLUSTERING: none. Every non-member is at 31.8 deg or more from the axis except nothing -- the nearest in angle is 75014 at 29.7 cm / 34.5 deg (0.3 cm, 2 points), and the two vertex protons sit at 177.6 deg, i.e. directly behind the start. NOT looked at: the 9 showers the scope rule skipped; 85025 is the only one above 20 MeV in the whole event. No pi0: no reco group, pio slots None, and the kine_pio_* block names an 8.3 + 412.4 MeV pair that no reconstruction accepted (correction 3 / the block's own warning). drag_check live: probe_radius_px 134, seg_u -51.01 -> -66.65, cloud_u -18.09 -> 18.46, cloud_redrew true.
